title.zh: 卷一百九十三 列傳第一百四十三: 列女
title.raw: 卷一百九十三 列傳第一百四十三: 列女 Volume 193 Biographies 143: Exemplary Women

sentences.zh: 女子稟陰柔之質，有從人之義。

translations.literal: Women receive the nature of yin and softness and have the duty of following others.
translations.idiomatic: Women are endowed with a yielding, feminine nature and are bound by the obligation to follow others.

sentences.zh: 前代誌貞婦烈女，蓋善其能以禮自防。

translations.literal: Former ages recorded chaste wives and fierce women, generally praising their ability to guard themselves through ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties recorded chaste wives and heroic women, chiefly to commend their power to protect themselves by observing ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 至若失身賊庭，不汙非義；

translations.literal: As for those who lost their persons in the rebel camp yet were not defiled by unrighteous conduct—
translations.idiomatic: Then there are those who fell into the power of rebel bands yet were not stained by wrongful acts—

sentences.zh: 臨白刃而慷慨，誓丹衷而激發；

translations.literal: they faced naked blades with lofty resolve and pledged their loyal hearts in passionate defiance;
translations.idiomatic: who faced naked blades with unflinching resolve and pledged their loyal hearts in passionate defiance;

sentences.zh: 粉身不顧，視死如歸，雖在壯夫，恐難守節，窈窕之操，不其賢乎！

translations.literal: they cared not if their bodies were ground to dust and regarded death as a homecoming; even stalwart men might struggle to keep such constancy—how worthy is the conduct of these gentle women!
translations.idiomatic: who thought nothing of being torn limb from limb and welcomed death as a homecoming—even strong men might fail to hold such constancy. How admirable is the moral fiber of these refined women!

sentences.zh: 其次梁鴻之妻，無辭偕隱，共姜之誓，不踐二庭，婦道母儀，克彰圖史，又其長也。

translations.literal: Next come Liang Hong's wife, who shared seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—their wifely virtue and maternal exemplars shine fully in the historical records, and this too is their excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Next are figures such as Liang Hong's wife, who followed her husband into seclusion without a word of protest, and Gong Jiang, who vowed never to enter a second household—their wifely virtue and maternal example are fully celebrated in the histories, and this too is their highest merit.

sentences.zh: 末代風靡，貞行寂寥，聊播椒蘭，以貽閨壺，彤管之職，幸無忽焉！

translations.literal: In the late age customs have declined and chaste conduct grown rare; I briefly scatter pepper and orchid to bestow upon the inner quarters—may the duty of the red brush not be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: In these latter days morals have declined and examples of constancy grown scarce; I offer here a brief bouquet of fragrant virtue for the women's quarters—may the historian's red brush never neglect this charge!

sentences.zh: 李德武妻裴氏，字淑英，戶部尚書、安邑公矩之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Dewu, née Pei, courtesy name Shuying, was the daughter of the Minister of Revenue and Duke of Anyi, Pei Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dewu's wife, Lady Pei, whose courtesy name was Shuying, was the daughter of Pei Ju, Minister of Revenue and Duke of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 性婉順有容德，事父母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Her nature was gentle and compliant, with dignified bearing; she was known for filial service to her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, compliant, and gracious in bearing, she was renowned for her filial devotion to her parents.

sentences.zh: 適德武，經一年而德武坐從父金才事徙嶺表。

translations.literal: She married Dewu; after one year Dewu was implicated in his cousin Jin Cai's affair and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After she married Dewu, within a year he was implicated in his cousin Jin Cai's crime and banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 矩時為黃門侍郎，奏請德武離婚，煬帝許之。

translations.literal: Ju was then Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and memorialized requesting that Dewu divorce her; Emperor Yang approved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ju was Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; he petitioned that Dewu divorce her, and Emperor Yang granted the request.

sentences.zh: 德武將與裴別，謂曰：「燕婉始爾，便事分離，方遠投瘴癘，恐無還理。

translations.literal: As Dewu was about to part from Pei he said, "We have only just begun our tender union, yet now we must separate; I am about to be cast far into malarial lands, and I fear there will be no return."
translations.idiomatic: When Dewu was about to leave Pei, he said, "We have only just begun our life together, yet we must part; I am being sent to the pestilent south, and I fear I shall never return."

sentences.zh: 尊君奏留，必欲改嫁耳，於此即事長訣矣！

translations.literal: "Your honored father has memorialized to keep you here; he surely intends you to remarry—this is our final farewell!"
translations.idiomatic: "Your father has petitioned to keep you here; he surely means for you to remarry. This is our final parting!"

sentences.zh: 」裴泣而對曰：「婦人事夫，無再醮之禮。

translations.literal: Pei wept and replied, "A wife serves her husband; there is no ritual of marrying again."
translations.idiomatic: Pei wept and answered, "A wife serves her husband; there is no ritual that permits a second marriage."

sentences.zh: 夫者，天也，何可背乎！

translations.literal: "The husband is Heaven—how could I turn against him!"
translations.idiomatic: "A husband is like Heaven itself—how could I turn against him!"

sentences.zh: 守之以死，必無他誌！

translations.literal: "I shall guard this unto death; I shall have no other intent!"
translations.idiomatic: "I shall hold to this unto death; I shall have no other purpose!"

sentences.zh: 」因操刀欲割耳自誓，保者禁之，乃止。

translations.literal: She then took up a knife intending to cut off her ear as a vow; her attendants restrained her and she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: She then seized a knife to cut off her ear as a vow of constancy; her attendants restrained her, and she desisted.

sentences.zh: 裴與德武別後，容貌毀悴，常讀佛經，不禦膏澤。

translations.literal: After Pei parted from Dewu her appearance was wasted and haggard; she constantly read Buddhist sutras and did not apply cosmetics.
translations.idiomatic: After parting from Dewu, Pei's appearance grew gaunt and careworn; she read Buddhist sutras constantly and wore no cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 李氏之姊妹在都邑者，歲時朔望，必命左右致敬而省焉。

translations.literal: For the sisters of the Li clan who were in the capital, at the seasonal new and full moons she always ordered her attendants to pay respects and inquire after them.
translations.idiomatic: For the Li sisters who lived in the capital, at each new and full moon she always had her attendants pay respects and inquire after their welfare.

sentences.zh: 裴又嘗讀《烈女傳》，見稱述不改嫁者，乃謂所親曰：「不踐二庭，婦人常理，何為以此載於記傳乎？

translations.literal: Pei also once read the Biographies of Fierce Women and, seeing praise for those who did not remarry, said to those close to her, "Not entering a second household is ordinary conduct for a woman—why record this in annals?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei once read the Biographies of Exemplary Women and, seeing praise for those who refused remarriage, remarked to her intimates, "Refusing a second marriage is ordinary conduct for a wife—why should such things be recorded in the histories?"

sentences.zh: 」後十余年間，與德武音信斷絕。

translations.literal: For more than ten years thereafter, all correspondence with Dewu was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years thereafter, all word from Dewu ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 矩欲奪其誌。

translations.literal: Ju wished to break her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sought to break her resolve.

sentences.zh: 時有柳直求婚，許之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zhi sought her hand in marriage, and Ju agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zhi proposed marriage, and Ju consented.

sentences.zh: 期有定日，乃以翦刀斷其發，悲泣絕粒。

translations.literal: When the wedding day was fixed, she cut off her hair with scissors, wept in grief, and refused food.
translations.idiomatic: When the wedding day was set, she cut off her hair with scissors, wept bitterly, and refused all food.

sentences.zh: 矩不可奪，乃止。

translations.literal: Ju could not change her mind and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Ju could not sway her, and the marriage was called off.

sentences.zh: 德武已於嶺表娶爾硃氏為妻，及遇赦得還，至襄州，聞裴守節，乃出其後妻，重與裴合。

translations.literal: Dewu had already taken Erzhu as wife in Lingnan; when he received amnesty and returned, reaching Xiangzhou he heard that Pei had kept her chastity, dismissed his later wife, and reunited with Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Dewu had meanwhile taken a woman named Erzhu as his wife in the south; when he was pardoned and returned, he reached Xiangzhou, learned that Pei had kept her vows, dismissed his second wife, and reunited with Pei.

sentences.zh: 生三男四女。

translations.literal: They bore three sons and four daughters.
translations.idiomatic: They had three sons and four daughters.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，德武終於鹿城令，裴歲余亦卒。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era Dewu died in office as magistrate of Lucheng; Pei died a little over a year later.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, Dewu died while serving as magistrate of Lucheng; Pei followed him in death a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 楊慶妻王氏，世充兄之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Yang Qing, née Wang, was the daughter of Wang Shichong's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing's wife, Lady Wang, was a daughter of Wang Shichong's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 慶即隋河間王弘之子。

translations.literal: Qing was the son of Hong, Prince of Hejian under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was the son of Hong, Prince of Hejian under the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 大業末，封郇王，為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xun and made Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xun and appointed Administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 後陷於世充。

translations.literal: Later he fell into Wang Shichong's hands.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell into Wang Shichong's power.

sentences.zh: 世充以兄女妻之，授管州刺史。

translations.literal: Shichong gave him his brother's daughter in marriage and appointed him Prefect of Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong gave him his niece in marriage and appointed him Prefect of Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及太宗攻圍洛陽，慶謀背世充，欲與其妻俱來歸國。

translations.literal: When Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to betray Shichong and wished to come over to the Tang together with his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to defect from Shichong and intended to surrender to the Tang together with his wife.

sentences.zh: 妻謂慶曰：「鄭國以妾奉箕帚於公者，所以結公心耳。

translations.literal: His wife said to Qing, "The State of Zheng gave me to you as broom and dustpan to win your heart."
translations.idiomatic: His wife said to Qing, "The State of Zheng gave me to you as wife precisely to bind your loyalty to them."

sentences.zh: 今既二三其行，負恩背義，自為身謀，妾將奈何？

translations.literal: "Now that you have shifted your conduct, betrayed favor and turned against righteousness, scheming for yourself—what am I to do?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now that you waver in your loyalty, betray their kindness, and plot only for yourself—what am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 若至長安，則公家之婢耳！

translations.literal: "If I reach Chang'an, I shall be merely a servant in your household!"
translations.idiomatic: "If I reach Chang'an, I shall be nothing but a servant in your house!"

sentences.zh: 願送至東都，公之惠也。

translations.literal: "I wish only to be sent to the Eastern Capital—that would be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask only that you send me to the Eastern Capital—that would be your one kindness to me."

sentences.zh: 」慶不聽。

translations.literal: Qing would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Qing refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 伺慶出後，謂侍者曰：「唐兵若勝，我家則戚。

translations.literal: When Qing had gone out, she said to her attendants, "If the Tang troops prevail, my family will be ruined."
translations.idiomatic: After Qing had gone out, she told her attendants, "If the Tang army wins, my family will be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 鄭國無危，吾夫又死，進退維谷。

translations.literal: "If the State of Zheng is unharmed, my husband will die; whether I advance or retreat I am trapped."
translations.idiomatic: "If Zheng survives, my husband will die for his treachery; whether I go forward or back, I am trapped."

sentences.zh: 何以生焉？

translations.literal: "How could I go on living?"
translations.idiomatic: "How could I go on living?"

sentences.zh: 」乃飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: She then took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 慶既入朝，官至宜州刺史。

translations.literal: After Qing entered court service he rose to Prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Qing entered Tang service, he rose to the post of Prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 時又有獨孤武都，謀叛王世充歸國，事覺誅死。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Dugu Wudu, who plotted to rebel against Wang Shichong and return to the Tang; the affair was discovered and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Dugu Wudu, who plotted to defect from Wang Shichong to the Tang; the plot was discovered and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 武都子師仁，年始三歲，世充以其年幼不殺，使禁掌之。

translations.literal: Wudu's son Shiren was only three years old; Shichong, because he was young, did not kill him but had him imprisoned and guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Wudu's son Shiren was only three years old; Shichong spared him because of his youth but had him imprisoned under guard.

sentences.zh: 乳母王氏，號蘭英，請髡鉗，求入保養，世充許之。

translations.literal: His wet nurse Wang, called Lanying, requested to be shaved and shackled in order to enter and care for him; Shichong granted this.
translations.idiomatic: His wet nurse, Lady Wang, known as Lanying, asked to be shorn and shackled so that she might enter the prison to care for him; Shichong consented.

sentences.zh: 蘭英撫育提攜，備盡筋力。

translations.literal: Lanying nursed and raised him, exhausting all her strength.
translations.idiomatic: Lanying nursed and raised him, giving every ounce of her strength.

sentences.zh: 時喪亂年饑，人多鋨死，蘭英扶路乞丐捃拾。

translations.literal: In those times of turmoil and famine many starved to death; Lanying supported herself along the roads, begging and gathering scraps.
translations.idiomatic: In those years of chaos and famine, when many starved to death, Lanying went begging along the roads and gathered whatever she could find.

sentences.zh: 遇有所得，便歸與師仁；

translations.literal: Whatever she obtained she brought back for Shiren;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever she obtained, she brought back for Shiren;

sentences.zh: 蘭英唯啖土飲水而已。

translations.literal: Lanying herself ate only earth and drank only water.
translations.idiomatic: Lanying herself ate only dirt and drank only water.

sentences.zh: 後詐采拾，乃竊師仁歸於京師。

translations.literal: Later, pretending to go gathering, she stole Shiren away and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, pretending to go out gathering, she stole Shiren away and fled with him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其義，下詔曰：「師仁乳母王氏，慈惠有聞，撫鞠無倦，提攜遺幼，背逆歸朝。

translations.literal: Gaozu commended her righteousness and issued an edict: "Shiren's wet nurse Wang is known for kindness and grace; she reared him without weariness, carried off the orphaned infant, and defied the rebel to return to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu commended her loyalty and issued an edict: "Shiren's wet nurse, Lady Wang, is renowned for her kindness and grace; she reared him without rest, carried off the orphaned child, and defied the rebel regime to bring him back to the court."

sentences.zh: 宜有褒隆，以錫其號。

translations.literal: "She should receive lofty commendation and be granted a title."
translations.idiomatic: "She deserves high honor and a title in recognition of her deeds."

sentences.zh: 可封永壽郡君」。

translations.literal: "She may be enfeoffed as Lady of Yongshou Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: "Let her be enfeoffed as Lady of Yongshou Commandery."

sentences.zh: 楊三安妻李氏，雍州涇陽人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Yang San'an, née Li, was a native of Jingyang in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang San'an's wife, Lady Li, was a native of Jingyang in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事舅姑以孝聞。

translations.literal: She was known for filial service to her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She was renowned for her filial devotion to her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及舅姑亡沒，三安亦死，二子孩童，家至貧窶。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law died, San'an also died, leaving two young sons; the household was utterly destitute.
translations.idiomatic: After her parents-in-law died, San'an died as well, leaving two young sons; the family was utterly destitute.

sentences.zh: 李晝則力田，夜紡緝，數年間葬舅姑及夫之叔侄兄弟者七喪，深為遠近所嗟尚。

translations.literal: Li worked the fields by day and spun at night; within several years she buried her parents-in-law and seven of her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers, and was deeply admired near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li worked the fields by day and spun cloth at night; within a few years she had buried her parents-in-law and seven of her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers, winning deep admiration throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而異之，賜帛二百段，遣州縣所在存恤之。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of this and was struck by it; he bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and ordered the local prefecture and county to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of this, he was deeply impressed; he granted her two hundred bolts of silk and ordered the local authorities to provide for her welfare.

sentences.zh: 魏衡妻王氏，梓州郪人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Wei Heng, née Wang, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng's wife, Lady Wang, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 武德初，薛仁杲舊將房企地侵掠梁郡，因獲王氏，逼而妻之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era, Fang Qidi, a former general of Xue Rengao, raided Liang Commandery, captured Wang, and forced her to become his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign, Fang Qidi, a former general of Xue Rengao, raided Liang Commandery, captured Lady Wang, and forced her to marry him.

sentences.zh: 後企地漸強盛，衡謀以城應賊。

translations.literal: Later, as Qidi grew increasingly powerful, Heng plotted to surrender the city to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As Qidi grew increasingly powerful, Heng plotted to surrender the city to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 企地領眾將趨梁州，未至數十里，飲酒醉臥。

translations.literal: Qidi led his troops toward Liangzhou; when they were still several tens of li away, he drank wine, became drunk, and lay down to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Qidi led his troops toward Liangzhou; when they were still several dozen li away, he drank himself into a stupor and fell asleep.

sentences.zh: 王氏取其佩刀斬之，攜其首入城，賊眾乃散。

translations.literal: Wang took his belt knife and slew him, carried his head into the city, and the rebel host dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang took his belt knife and killed him, carried his head into the city, and the rebel forces scattered.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，封為崇義夫人，舍衡同賊之罪。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased, enfeoffed her as Lady of Chongyi, and pardoned Heng's crime of colluding with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased; he enfeoffed her as Lady of Chongyi and pardoned Heng for his collusion with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 樊會仁母敬氏，字像子，蒲州河東人也。

translations.literal: The mother of Fan Huiren, née Jing, courtesy name Xiangzi, was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Huiren's mother, Lady Jing, whose courtesy name was Xiangzi, was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十五，適樊氏，生會仁而夫喪，事舅姑姊姒以謹順聞。

translations.literal: At fifteen she married into the Fan clan, bore Huiren, and when her husband died she was known for dutiful and compliant service to her parents-in-law and sisters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen she married into the Fan clan and bore Huiren; after her husband's death she was renowned for her dutiful and respectful care of her parents-in-law and sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及服終，母兄以其盛年，將奪其誌。

translations.literal: When her mourning was complete, her mother and elder brother, because she was still in her prime, intended to break her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When her mourning period ended, her mother and elder brother, seeing that she was still young, sought to make her remarry.

sentences.zh: 微加諷諭，便悲恨嗚咽，如此者數四。

translations.literal: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep and sob in grief, and this happened four or five times.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep and sob in grief; this happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 母兄乃潛許人為婚，矯稱母患以召之。

translations.literal: Her mother and brother then secretly betrothed her to another man and falsely claimed that her mother was ill to summon her.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother and brother then secretly betrothed her to another man and summoned her home with a false report that her mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 凡所營具，皆寄之鄰裏。

translations.literal: All the wedding preparations were stored with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: All the wedding preparations were stored with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 像子既至，省母無疾，鄰家復具肴善，像子知為所欺，佯為不悟者。

translations.literal: When Xiangzi arrived and found her mother had no illness, the neighbors again set out fine dishes; Xiangzi knew she had been deceived and pretended not to understand.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangzi arrived and found her mother was not ill, the neighbors again set out a feast; Xiangzi realized she had been deceived and pretended not to notice.

sentences.zh: 其嫂復請像子沐浴。

translations.literal: Her sister-in-law again asked Xiangzi to bathe.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister-in-law then asked Xiangzi to bathe.

sentences.zh: 像子私謂會仁曰：「吾不幸孀居，誓與汝父同穴。

translations.literal: Xiangzi privately told Huiren, "I am unfortunate in my widowhood and have sworn to share a grave with your father."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzi privately told Huiren, "I am unfortunate in my widowhood and have sworn to share a grave with your father."

sentences.zh: 所以不死者，徒以我母羸老，汝身幼弱。

translations.literal: "The reason I have not died is only that my mother is frail and aged and you are young and weak."
translations.idiomatic: "The only reason I have not died is that my mother is frail and aged, and you are still young and helpless."

sentences.zh: 今汝舅欲奪吾誌，將加逼迫，於汝何如！

translations.literal: "Now your uncle wishes to break my resolve and will force me—what will become of you!"
translations.idiomatic: "Now your uncle wishes to break my vow and will force me to remarry—what will become of you then!"

sentences.zh: 」會仁失聲啼泣。

translations.literal: Huiren burst into loud weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Huiren burst into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 像子撫之曰：「汝勿啼。

translations.literal: Xiangzi comforted him and said, "Do not weep."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzi comforted him and said, "Do not cry."

sentences.zh: 吾向偽不覺者，令汝舅不我為意。

translations.literal: "I pretended not to notice earlier so that your uncle would not be on his guard against me."
translations.idiomatic: "I pretended not to notice earlier so that your uncle would not be on his guard."

sentences.zh: 聞汝啼，知吾覺悟，必加妨備，則吾難為計矣！

translations.literal: "If he hears you weeping he will know I have understood and will surely take precautions—then my plan will be hard to carry out!"
translations.idiomatic: "If he hears you crying, he will know I have understood and will surely take precautions—then I shall have no way to escape!"

sentences.zh: 」會仁便佯睡，像子於是伺隙攜之遁歸。

translations.literal: Huiren then pretended to sleep, and Xiangzi seized an opportunity to take him and flee home.
translations.idiomatic: Huiren then pretended to sleep; Xiangzi seized her chance, took him, and fled home.

sentences.zh: 中路，兄使追及之，將逼與俱返。

translations.literal: Midway her brother sent men to overtake them and was about to force them to return together.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way her brother sent men to overtake them and tried to force them to return.

sentences.zh: 像子誓以必死，辭情甚切，其兄感嘆而止。

translations.literal: Xiangzi vowed she would die rather than comply; her words were most earnest, and her brother sighed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzi swore she would die rather than comply; her words were so earnest that her brother sighed and let them go.

sentences.zh: 後會仁年十八病卒，時像子母已終。

translations.literal: Later, when Huiren was eighteen he died of illness; by then Xiangzi's mother had already passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Huiren was eighteen, he died of illness; by then Xiangzi's mother had already died.

sentences.zh: 既葬，像子謂其所親曰：「吾老母不幸，又夫死子亡，義無久活。

translations.literal: After the burial Xiangzi said to those close to her, "My aged mother has passed away, and my husband is dead and my son lost—there is no righteousness in living long."
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, Xiangzi told her intimates, "My mother is gone, my husband is dead, and my son is lost—there is no reason left to live."

sentences.zh: 」於是號慟不食，數日而死。

translations.literal: She then wailed in grief and refused food, dying within several days.
translations.idiomatic: She then wailed in grief and refused all food, dying within a few days.

sentences.zh: 絳州孝女衛氏，字無忌，夏縣人也。

translations.literal: The filial daughter of Jiangzhou, née Wei, courtesy name Wuji, was a native of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: The filial daughter of Jiang Prefecture, Lady Wei, whose courtesy name was Wuji, was a native of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 初，其父為鄉人衛長則所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier her father had been killed by a fellow townsman, Wei Changze.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had earlier been killed by a fellow townsman named Wei Changze.

sentences.zh: 無忌年六歲，母又改嫁，無兄弟。

translations.literal: Wuji was six years old; her mother remarried, and she had no brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was six at the time; her mother remarried, and she had no brothers.

sentences.zh: 及長，常思復仇。

translations.literal: When she grew up she constantly thought of taking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up, she constantly brooded on revenge.

sentences.zh: 無忌從伯常設宴為樂，長則時亦預坐，無忌以磚擊殺之。

translations.literal: Wuji's uncle by the father's line often held banquets for pleasure; Changze would sometimes attend, and Wuji killed him with a brick.
translations.idiomatic: Her father's elder cousin often held banquets for pleasure; Changze would sometimes attend, and Wuji killed him with a brick.

sentences.zh: 既而詣吏，稱父仇既報，請就刑戮。

translations.literal: She then went to the officials, declaring that her father's enemy had been avenged and asking to submit to execution.
translations.idiomatic: She then went to the magistrate, declared that her father's murder had been avenged, and asked to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 巡察大使、黃門侍郎褚遂良以聞，太宗嘉其孝烈，特令免罪，給傳乘徙於雍州，並給田宅，仍令州縣以禮嫁之。

translations.literal: The touring inspector and Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Chu Suiliang reported this; Taizong commended her filial heroism, specially ordered her pardoned, provided relay horses to move her to Yongzhou, granted fields and a residence, and further ordered the prefecture and county to marry her off with proper ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The touring inspector and Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Chu Suiliang reported the matter; Emperor Taizong commended her filial heroism, specially pardoned her, provided relay horses to relocate her to Yong Prefecture, granted her fields and a residence, and ordered the local authorities to provide her with a proper marriage.

sentences.zh: 孝女賈氏，濮州鄄城人也。

translations.literal: The filial daughter Jia was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The filial daughter Jia was a native of Juancheng in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年始十五，其父為宗人玄基所害。

translations.literal: When she was only fifteen her father was killed by a clansman, Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: When she was only fifteen, her father was murdered by a clansman named Xuanji.

sentences.zh: 其弟強仁年幼，賈氏撫育之，誓以不嫁。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Qiangren was young; Jia raised him and vowed never to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Qiangren was still a child; Jia raised him and vowed never to marry.

sentences.zh: 及強仁成童，思共報復，乃俟玄基殺之；

translations.literal: When Qiangren came of age they planned revenge together; they waited for an opportunity and killed Xuanji;
translations.idiomatic: When Qiangren came of age, they plotted revenge together; they lay in wait and killed Xuanji;

sentences.zh: 取其心肝，以祭父墓。

translations.literal: took his heart and liver, and used them to sacrifice at their father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: cut out his heart and liver and offered them at their father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 遣強仁自列於縣，司斷以極刑。

translations.literal: They sent Qiangren to present himself at the county; the authorities sentenced him to the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Qiangren to turn himself in at the county seat; the authorities sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 賈氏詣闕自陳己為，請代強仁死。

translations.literal: Jia went to the court to declare her own guilt and asked to die in Qiangren's place.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jia went to the capital to confess her own guilt and asked to die in Qiangren's place.

sentences.zh: 高宗哀之，特下制賈氏及強仁免罪，移其家於洛陽。

translations.literal: Gaozong pitied them and specially issued an edict pardoning Jia and Qiangren and moving their household to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong took pity on them and specially issued an edict pardoning both Jia and Qiangren and relocating their family to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 鄭義宗妻盧氏，幽州范陽人，盧彥衡之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Zheng Yizong, née Lu, was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and the daughter of Lu Yanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yizong's wife, Lady Lu, was a native of Fanyang in You Prefecture and the daughter of Lu Yanheng.

sentences.zh: 略涉書史，事舅姑甚得婦道。

translations.literal: She had some acquaintance with books and histories and served her parents-in-law in a manner fully conforming to wifely conduct.
translations.idiomatic: She had some knowledge of literature and history and served her parents-in-law with exemplary wifely devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜有強盜數十人，持杖鼓噪，逾垣而入，家人悉奔竄，唯有姑獨在室。

translations.literal: Once at night several dozen bandits, wielding clubs and making a clamor, climbed over the wall and entered; the household all fled in panic, and only her mother-in-law remained alone in the room.
translations.idiomatic: One night several dozen bandits, brandishing clubs and raising a din, climbed over the wall; the entire household fled in panic, leaving only her mother-in-law alone in the room.

sentences.zh: 盧冒白刃往至姑側，為賊捶擊之，幾至於死。

translations.literal: Lu braved naked blades to go to her mother-in-law's side and was beaten by the bandits, nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lu braved naked blades to reach her mother-in-law's side and was beaten by the bandits nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 賊去後，家人問曰：「群兇擾橫，人盡奔逃，何獨不懼？

translations.literal: After the bandits left, her family asked, "When the violent criminals were rampaging and everyone fled, why alone were you not afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits left, her family asked, "When those violent men were rampaging and everyone fled, why were you alone not afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「人所以異於禽獸者，以其仁義也。

translations.literal: She answered, "What distinguishes humans from beasts and birds is their benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "What distinguishes human beings from beasts is benevolence and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 昔宋伯姬守義赴火，流稱至今。

translations.literal: In former times Lady Bo Ji of Song upheld righteousness and went into the flames; her fame flows down to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times Lady Bo Ji of Song upheld righteousness and walked into the flames; her fame endures to this day.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不敏，安敢忘義！

translations.literal: "Though I am not clever, how dare I forget righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: "Though I am not clever, how could I abandon righteousness!"

sentences.zh: 且鄰裏有急，尚相赴救，況在於姑，而可委棄！

translations.literal: "Moreover, when neighbors are in distress, one still goes to their rescue—how much more when it concerns one's mother-in-law could one abandon her!"
translations.idiomatic: "When neighbors are in distress, people still rush to help—how much less could I abandon my mother-in-law!"

sentences.zh: 若萬一危禍，豈宜獨生！

translations.literal: "If by any chance disaster should come, how could I live on alone!"
translations.idiomatic: "If disaster should strike, how could I survive alone!"

sentences.zh: 」其姑每嘆云：「古人稱歲寒然後知松柏之後雕也，吾今乃知盧新婦之心矣！

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law would often sigh and say, "The ancients said that only in cold years does one know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither—I now know the heart of my new daughter-in-law Lu!"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law would often sigh and say, "The ancients said that only in bitter cold does one know that the pine and cypress are the last to fade—I now truly know the heart of my daughter-in-law Lu!"

sentences.zh: 」貞觀中卒。

translations.literal: She died during the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: She died during the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 劉寂妻夏侯氏，滑州胙城人，字碎金。

translations.literal: The wife of Liu Ji, née Xiahou, was a native of Zuocheng in Huazhou; her courtesy name was Suijin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji's wife, Lady Xiahou, was a native of Zuocheng in Hua Prefecture; her courtesy name was Suijin.

sentences.zh: 父長雲，為鹽城縣丞，因疾喪明。

translations.literal: Her father Changyun was Assistant Magistrate of Yancheng County and lost his sight through illness.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Changyun served as Assistant Magistrate of Yancheng County and went blind from illness.

sentences.zh: 碎金乃求離其夫，以終侍養。

translations.literal: Suijin then sought to leave her husband in order to devote herself entirely to caring for him.
translations.idiomatic: Suijin then sought to leave her husband so that she could devote herself entirely to caring for her father.

sentences.zh: 經十五年，兼事後母，以至孝聞。

translations.literal: For fifteen years she also served her stepmother and was known for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: For fifteen years she also cared for her stepmother and was renowned for her filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，毀瘠殆不勝喪，被髮徒跣，負土成墳，廬於墓側，每日一食，如此者積年。

translations.literal: When her father died she was so emaciated by grief that she could scarcely bear the mourning; with hair unbound and barefoot she carried earth to build the tomb, dwelt in a hut beside the grave, and ate only one meal a day—thus for many years.
translations.idiomatic: When her father died, she was so wasted by grief that she could scarcely endure the mourning; with hair unbound and barefoot, she carried earth to build the tomb, lived in a hut beside the grave, and ate only one meal a day—for many years.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，有制表其門閭，賜以粟帛。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era an edict honored her household gate and bestowed grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, an edict honored her household and granted her grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 楊紹宗妻王氏，華州華陰人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Yang Shaozong, née Wang, was a native of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shaozong's wife, Lady Wang, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，年二歲，所生母亡，為繼母鞠養。

translations.literal: At first, when she was two years old, her birth mother died and she was raised by her stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: When she was two, her birth mother died, and she was raised by her stepmother.

sentences.zh: 至年十五，父又征遼而歿。

translations.literal: When she reached fifteen her father also died campaigning in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When she was fifteen, her father died on campaign in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 繼母尋亦卒。

translations.literal: Her stepmother soon died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Her stepmother soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 王乃收所生及繼母屍柩，並立父形像，招魂遷葬訖，廬於墓側，陪其祖父母及父母墳。

translations.literal: Wang then gathered the coffins of her birth mother and stepmother, set up her father's image, summoned his soul and reburied him, then dwelt in a hut beside the tomb, keeping vigil at the graves of her grandparents and parents.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang then gathered the coffins of her birth mother and stepmother, erected her father's portrait, summoned his soul and gave him a proper burial, then lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb, keeping vigil at the graves of her grandparents and parents.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，詔曰：「故楊紹宗妻王氏，因心為孝，率性成道。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era an edict stated, "The late wife of Yang Shaozong, née Wang, took filial piety from the heart and followed her nature to achieve the Way."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign, an edict stated, "The late Yang Shaozong's wife, Lady Wang, took filial piety from the heart and followed her nature to achieve moral perfection."

sentences.zh: 年迫桑榆，筋力衰謝。

translations.literal: "Her years approach the mulberry and elm sunset; her strength has declined."
translations.idiomatic: "Now in the twilight of her years, her strength has waned."

sentences.zh: 以往在隋朝，父歿遼左，招魂遷葬，負土成墳，又葬其祖父母等，遏此老年，親加板築。

translations.literal: "In former days under the Sui, when her father died in Liaodong she summoned his soul and reburied him, carried earth to build the tomb, and also buried her grandparents and others; despite her advanced age she personally laid the boards for the tomb construction."
translations.idiomatic: "Long ago under the Sui, when her father died in Liaodong, she summoned his soul home for burial, carried earth to build his tomb, and also buried her grandparents; despite her advanced age, she personally worked on the tomb construction."

sentences.zh: 痛結晨昏，哀感行路。

translations.literal: "Her grief bound morning and evening; her sorrow moved passersby on the road."
translations.idiomatic: "Her grief was unceasing; her sorrow moved all who passed by."

sentences.zh: 永言誌行，嘉尚良深。

translations.literal: "Her resolve and conduct merit the deepest commendation."
translations.idiomatic: "Her resolve and conduct deserve the highest praise."

sentences.zh: 宜標其門閭，用旌敏德。

translations.literal: "Her household gate should be honored to display her quick virtue."
translations.idiomatic: "Her household should be honored to display her exemplary virtue."

sentences.zh: 」賜物三十段、粟五十石。

translations.literal: She was granted thirty bolts of goods and fifty shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted thirty bolts of goods and fifty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 於敏直妻張氏，營州都督、皖城公儉之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Yu Minzhi, née Zhang, was the daughter of Jian, Regional Commander of Yingzhou and Duke of Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Minzhi's wife, Lady Zhang, was the daughter of Jian, Regional Commander of Yingzhou and Duke of Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 數歲時父母權有疾，即觀察顏色，不離左右，晝夜省侍，宛若成人。

translations.literal: When she was only a few years old, whenever her parents Quan fell ill she would observe their expressions, never leave their side, and attend them day and night like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood, whenever her parents fell ill, she watched their expressions, never left their side, and attended them day and night with the care of an adult.

sentences.zh: 及稍成長，恭順彌甚。

translations.literal: As she grew somewhat older her respect and compliance became even greater.
translations.idiomatic: As she grew older, her respect and obedience became even more pronounced.

sentences.zh: 適延壽公於欽明子敏直。

translations.literal: She married Minzhi, son of Qinming of the Duke of Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: She married Minzhi, son of Qinming of the Duke of Yanshou line.

sentences.zh: 初聞儉有疾，便即號踴自傷，期於必死。

translations.literal: When she first heard that Jian was ill she immediately wailed and stamped in grief, expecting she would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: When she first heard that Jian was ill, she immediately wailed and stamped in grief, fully expecting to die herself.

sentences.zh: 儉卒後，兇問至，號哭一慟而絕。

translations.literal: After Jian died, when the news of mourning arrived she wailed once in grief and lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Jian's death arrived, she wailed once in grief and lost consciousness.

sentences.zh: 高宗下詔，賜物百段，仍令史官錄之。

translations.literal: Gaozong issued an edict granting her one hundred bolts of goods and further ordered the historiographers to record it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong issued an edict granting her one hundred bolts of goods and ordered the historiographers to record her story.

sentences.zh: 冀州鹿城女子王阿足者，早孤，無兄弟，唯姊一人。

translations.literal: The woman Wang Azu of Lucheng in Jizhou was orphaned early, had no brothers, and only one elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Azu of Lucheng in Ji Prefecture was orphaned early, had no brothers, and only one elder sister.

sentences.zh: 阿足初適同縣李氏，未有子而夫亡。

translations.literal: Azu first married a man of the Li clan in the same county; she had no children when her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: Azu first married a man of the Li clan in the same county; she had no children when her husband died.

sentences.zh: 時年尚少，人多聘之。

translations.literal: She was still young and many sought her hand in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: She was still young, and many men sought her hand in marriage.

sentences.zh: 為姊年老孤寡，不能舍去，乃誓不嫁，以養其姊。

translations.literal: Because her sister was aged, widowed, and alone, she could not abandon her; she vowed never to marry and supported her sister.
translations.idiomatic: Because her sister was elderly, widowed, and alone, she could not abandon her; she vowed never to marry and devoted herself to supporting her sister.

sentences.zh: 每晝營田業，夜便紡績，衣食所須，無非阿足出者，如此二十余年。

translations.literal: Each day she worked the fields; each night she spun; all clothing and food needed came from Azu alone—thus for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Each day she worked the fields; each night she spun cloth; everything her sister needed came from Azu alone—for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 及姊喪，葬送以禮。

translations.literal: When her sister died she buried and sent her off with proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When her sister died, she buried her with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 鄉人莫不稱其節行，競令妻女求與相識。

translations.literal: The villagers all praised her chaste conduct and vied to have their wives and daughters seek her acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers all praised her constancy and urged their wives and daughters to seek her acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，竟終於家。

translations.literal: Several years later she finally died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later she died at home.

sentences.zh: 樊彥琛妻魏氏，楚州淮陰人。

translations.literal: The wife of Fan Yanchen, née Wei, was a native of Huaiyin in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanchen's wife, Lady Wei, was a native of Huaiyin in Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彥琛病篤，將卒，魏泣而言曰：「幸以愚陋，托身明德，奉侍衣裳，二十余載。

translations.literal: When Yanchen's illness was grave and he was about to die, Wei wept and said, "Fortunately, though foolish and lowly, I entrusted myself to your bright virtue and served your garments for more than twenty years."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchen's illness grew grave and death approached, Wei wept and said, "Though I am foolish and lowly, I have been fortunate to serve you for more than twenty years."

sentences.zh: 豈意釁妨所招，遽見此禍。

translations.literal: "Who would have thought that the offense I provoked would bring this calamity so suddenly."
translations.idiomatic: "I never imagined that misfortune would strike so suddenly."

sentences.zh: 同入黃泉，是其願也。

translations.literal: "To enter the yellow springs together—that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: "To enter the underworld together—that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 」彥琛答曰：「死生常道，無所多恨。

translations.literal: Yanchen answered, "Life and death are the constant way; there is nothing much to regret."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchen answered, "Life and death follow the natural order; I have little to regret."

sentences.zh: 君宜勉勵，養諸孤，使其成立。

translations.literal: "You should strive on, raise the orphans, and see that they are established."
translations.idiomatic: "You must persevere, raise our orphans, and see that they grow to maturity."

sentences.zh: 若相從而死，適足貽累，非吾所取也。

translations.literal: "If you follow me in death you will only add to the burden—that is not what I would choose."
translations.idiomatic: "If you die with me, you will only add to their burden—that is not what I wish."

sentences.zh: 」彥琛卒後，屬李敬業之亂，乃為賊所獲。

translations.literal: After Yanchen died, during Li Jingye's rebellion she was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanchen died, during Li Jingye's rebellion she was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊黨知其素解絲竹，逼令彈箏。

translations.literal: The rebel band knew she was skilled in string and wind music and forced her to play the zither.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels knew she was skilled in music and forced her to play the zither.

sentences.zh: 魏氏嘆曰：「我夫不幸亡歿，未能自盡，茍復偷生。

translations.literal: Wei sighed and said, "My husband unfortunately died; I could not end my own life and have clung to life in degradation."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei sighed and said, "My husband died; I could not follow him in death and have clung to life in shame."

sentences.zh: 今爾見逼管弦，豈非禍從手發耶？

translations.literal: "Now that you force me to play strings and pipes, is this not disaster issuing from my own hands?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now you force me to play music—is not disaster issuing from my own hands?"

sentences.zh: 」乃引刀斬指，棄之於地。

translations.literal: She then took a knife and cut off her finger, casting it on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: She then took a knife and cut off her finger, casting it on the ground.

sentences.zh: 賊黨又欲妻之，魏以必死自固。

translations.literal: The rebels also wished to take her as wife; Wei held firm with the resolve to die.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also wished to take her as wife; Wei held firm with the resolve to die.

sentences.zh: 賊等忿怒，以刃加頸，語云：「若不從我，即當殞命。

translations.literal: The rebels grew furious, placed blades to her neck, and said, "If you do not obey us, you shall perish at once."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew furious, placed blades to her neck, and said, "If you do not obey us, you shall die at once."

sentences.zh: 」乃厲聲罵曰：「爾等狗盜，乃欲汙辱好人，今得速死，會我本誌。

translations.literal: She then cursed them in a fierce voice, "You dog-thieves wish to defile a good person—now I can die quickly, which accords with my original intent."
translations.idiomatic: She cursed them fiercely: "You dog-thieves wish to defile an honorable woman—now I can die quickly, which fulfills my original intent."

sentences.zh: 」賊乃斬之，聞者莫不傷惜。

translations.literal: The rebels then beheaded her; all who heard of it grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then beheaded her; all who heard of it mourned her loss.

sentences.zh: 鄒保英妻奚氏，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Zou Baoying, née Xi, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Baoying's wife, Lady Xi, was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，契丹賊李盡忠來寇平州。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebel Li Jinzhong came to raid Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian reign, the Khitan rebel Li Jinzhong invaded Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 保英時任刺史，領兵討擊。

translations.literal: Baoying was then serving as prefect and led troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying was then serving as prefect and led troops to repel the invasion.

sentences.zh: 既而城孤援寡，勢將欲陷。

translations.literal: Soon the city was isolated with few reinforcements and the situation was about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city was isolated with few reinforcements and was on the verge of falling.

sentences.zh: 奚氏乃率家僮及城內女丁相助固守。

translations.literal: Xi then led household servants and the women of the city to help defend and hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi then led household servants and the women of the city to help defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 賊退，所司以聞，優制封為誠節夫人。

translations.literal: When the rebels retreated the authorities reported it; by special edict she was enfeoffed as Lady of Sincere Constancy.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels retreated, the authorities reported her deeds; by special edict she was enfeoffed as Lady of Sincere Constancy.

sentences.zh: 時有古玄應妻高氏，亦能固守飛狐縣城，卒免為突厥所陷。

translations.literal: At the same time the wife of Gu Xuanying, née Gao, was also able to hold firm the walls of Feihu County and ultimately escaped being captured by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, Gu Xuanying's wife, Lady Gao, also held firm the walls of Feihu County and ultimately prevented its capture by the Turks.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「頃屬默啜攻城，鹹憂陷沒。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Recently, when Moqi besieged cities, all feared they would fall."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "Recently, when Moqi besieged our cities, all feared they would fall."

sentences.zh: 丈夫固守，猶不能堅，婦人懷忠，不憚流矢；

translations.literal: "Men holding firm still could not stand fast, yet women bearing loyalty did not fear flying arrows;"
translations.idiomatic: "Men defending the walls could not hold firm, yet women bearing loyal hearts did not fear flying arrows;"

sentences.zh: 由茲感激，危城重安。

translations.literal: "through such stirring devotion, endangered cities were restored to safety."
translations.idiomatic: "through such stirring devotion, endangered cities were restored to safety."

sentences.zh: 如不褒升，何以獎勸！

translations.literal: "If we do not reward and promote them, how can we encourage and exhort!"
translations.idiomatic: "If we do not reward them, how can we encourage such virtue!"

sentences.zh: 古玄應妻可封為徇忠縣君。」

translations.literal: "The wife of Gu Xuanying may be enfeoffed as Lady of Xunzhong County."
translations.idiomatic: "Gu Xuanying's wife shall be enfeoffed as Lady of Xunzhong County."

sentences.zh: 宋庭瑜妻魏氏，定州鼓城人，隋著作郎彥泉之後也。

translations.literal: The wife of Song Tingyu, née Wei, was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou and a descendant of Yanquan, Editorial Director under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Song Tingyu's wife, Lady Wei, was a native of Gucheng in Ding Prefecture and a descendant of Yanquan, Editorial Director under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 世為山東士族。

translations.literal: For generations her family had been a Shandong gentry clan.
translations.idiomatic: Her family had been a Shandong gentry clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 父克己，有詞學，則天時為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: Her father Keji was skilled in literary composition; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Keji was skilled in literary composition; during Empress Wu's reign he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 魏氏善屬文。

translations.literal: Wei was skilled at composing literary works.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 先天中，庭瑜自司農少卿左遷涪州別駕。

translations.literal: During the Xiantian era Tingyu was demoted from Vice Minister of Agriculture to Assistant Administrator of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian reign, Tingyu was demoted from Vice Minister of Agriculture to Assistant Administrator of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魏氏隨夫之任，中路作《南征賦》以敘誌，詞甚典美。

translations.literal: Wei accompanied her husband to his post; midway she composed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to record her thoughts, and the language was most elegant and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei accompanied her husband to his post; along the way she composed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to record her thoughts, and its language was elegant and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 開元中，庭瑜累遷慶州都督。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era Tingyu was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, Tingyu was promoted to Regional Commander of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，中書令張說年少時為克己所重，魏氏恨其夫為外職，乃作書與說，敘亡父疇昔之事，並為庭瑜申理，乃錄《南征賦》寄說。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Yue was Chief Minister of the Secretariat, in his youth he had been valued by Keji; Wei resented that her husband held an outer post, so she wrote a letter to Yue recounting her late father's affairs of former days and pleading Tingyu's case, and enclosed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to send to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chief Minister Zhang Yue had been valued by Keji in his youth; resenting her husband's exile to a distant post, Lady Wei wrote to Yue recounting her late father's past kindness and pleading Tingyu's case, enclosing the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition."

sentences.zh: 說嘆曰：「曹大家《東征》之流也。

translations.literal: Yue sighed and said, "This is in the vein of Lady Cao's 'Eastern Expedition.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yue sighed and said, "This is in the vein of Lady Cao Ban's 'Eastern Expedition.'"

sentences.zh: 」庭瑜尋轉廣州都督，道病卒。

translations.literal: Tingyu was soon transferred to Regional Commander of Guangzhou but died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu was soon transferred to Regional Commander of Guang Prefecture but died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 魏氏旬日亦殞，時人莫不傷之。

translations.literal: Wei also died within ten days; people of the time all grieved for them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei died within ten days as well; all who heard of it mourned their loss.

sentences.zh: 崔繪妻盧氏，幽州范陽人也，為山東著姓。

translations.literal: The wife of Cui Hui, née Lu, was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and a prominent Shandong surname.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hui's wife, Lady Lu, was a native of Fanyang in You Prefecture and a prominent Shandong clan.

sentences.zh: 祖幼孫，常州刺史。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Yousun was Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Yousun served as Prefect of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父獻，有美名，則天時歷鸞臺侍郎、文昌左丞。

translations.literal: Her father Xian had a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Vice Director of the Literary Glory Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xian enjoyed a fine reputation; during Empress Wu's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Vice Director of the Literary Glory Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天授中為酷吏來俊臣所陷，左遷西鄉令而卒。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he was framed by the cruel official Lai Junchen, demoted to Magistrate of Xixiang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou reign he was framed by the cruel official Lai Junchen, demoted to Magistrate of Xixiang, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 繪早終，盧既年少，諸兄常欲嫁之。

translations.literal: Hui died early; Lu was still young and her elder brothers often wished to marry her off.
translations.idiomatic: Hui died young; Lu was still young, and her elder brothers often wished to marry her off.

sentences.zh: 盧輒稱病固辭。

translations.literal: Lu would repeatedly claim illness and firmly refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Lu would repeatedly claim illness and firmly refuse.

sentences.zh: 盧亡姊之夫李思沖，神龍初為工部侍郎，又求續親。

translations.literal: Lu's deceased elder sister's husband Li Sichong, in the early Shenlong era serving as Vice Minister of Works, again sought to continue the marriage tie.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's deceased elder sister's husband, Li Sichong, who in the early Shenlong reign served as Vice Minister of Works, again sought to marry her.

sentences.zh: 時思沖當朝美職，諸兄不之拒。

translations.literal: At the time Sichong held a fine post at court and her brothers did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sichong held a prestigious post at court, and her brothers did not refuse.

sentences.zh: 將婚之夕，方以告盧；

translations.literal: On the eve of the wedding they finally told Lu;
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the wedding, they finally told Lu;

sentences.zh: 盧又固辭不可，仍令人防其門。

translations.literal: Lu again firmly refused and could not be moved; they still had people guard her door.
translations.idiomatic: Lu again firmly refused; they had people guard her door.

sentences.zh: 盧謂左右曰：「吾自誓久已定矣！

translations.literal: Lu said to those around her, "My vow was settled long ago!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu told her attendants, "My vow was settled long ago!"

sentences.zh: 」乃夜中出自竇中，奔歸崔氏，發面盡為糞穢所汙。

translations.literal: She then in the middle of the night went out through a hole in the wall and fled back to the Cui household; her hair and face were entirely fouled with excrement.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the night she crawled out through a hole in the wall and fled back to the Cui household; her hair and face were smeared with filth.

sentences.zh: 宗族見者皆為之垂淚。

translations.literal: All of her clan who saw her wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: All of her clan who saw her wept for her.

sentences.zh: 因出家為尼，諸尼欽其操行，皆尊事之。

translations.literal: She then left home to become a nun; the nuns admired her conduct and all honored and served her.
translations.idiomatic: She then became a nun; the other nuns admired her conduct and all honored her.

sentences.zh: 開元中，以老病而卒。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era she died of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign she died of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 奉天縣竇氏二女伯娘、仲娘，雖長於村野，而幼有誌操。

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Dou clan of Fengtian County, Boniang and Zhongniang, though raised in the countryside, from youth possessed resolute conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters of the Dou clan of Fengtian County, Boniang and Zhongniang, though raised in the countryside, possessed resolute moral character from youth.

sentences.zh: 住與邠州接界。

translations.literal: Their dwelling bordered Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They lived on the border with Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，草賊數千人，持兵刃入其村落行剽劫，聞二女有容色，姊年十九，妹年十六，藏於巖窟間。

translations.literal: During the Yongtai era several thousand bandits, bearing weapons, entered their village to plunder; hearing the two sisters were beautiful—the elder nineteen, the younger sixteen—they hid in a rocky cave.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongtai reign, several thousand bandits armed with weapons raided their village; hearing that the two sisters were beautiful—the elder nineteen, the younger sixteen—they hid in a rocky cave.

sentences.zh: 賊徒擬為逼辱，乃先曳伯娘出，行數十步，又曳仲娘出，賊相顧自慰。

translations.literal: The bandits intended to force and dishonor them; they first dragged Boniang out, walked several tens of paces, then dragged Zhongniang out; the bandits looked at one another in self-congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits intended to violate them; they first dragged Boniang out, walked several dozen paces, then dragged Zhongniang out; the bandits exchanged satisfied glances.

sentences.zh: 行臨深谷，伯娘曰：「我豈受賊汙辱！

translations.literal: As they came to a deep ravine, Boniang said, "How could I suffer defilement by bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: As they reached a deep ravine, Boniang cried, "I would never suffer defilement at the hands of bandits!"

sentences.zh: 」乃投之於谷。

translations.literal: She then cast herself into the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the ravine.

sentences.zh: 賊方驚駭，仲娘又投於谷。

translations.literal: The bandits were just startled when Zhongniang also threw herself into the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were still startled when Zhongniang threw herself into the ravine as well.

sentences.zh: 谷深數百尺，姊尋卒；

translations.literal: The ravine was several hundred feet deep; the elder sister soon died;
translations.idiomatic: The ravine was hundreds of feet deep; the elder sister died immediately;

sentences.zh: 仲娘腳折面破，血流被體，氣絕良久而蘇，賊義之而去。

translations.literal: Zhongniang's legs were broken and her face shattered, blood soaking her body; she lost breath for a long time then revived; the bandits, moved by righteousness, left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongniang's legs were broken and her face shattered, blood soaking her body; she lost consciousness for a long time but revived; moved by her courage, the bandits departed.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹第五琦感其貞烈，奏之；

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor Diwu Qi, moved by their chaste heroism, memorialized the matter;
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Diwu Qi, moved by their chaste heroism, memorialized the matter;

sentences.zh: 詔旌表門閭，長免丁役，二女葬事官給。

translations.literal: an edict honored their household gate, permanently exempted corvée labor, and provided official funds for the two daughters' burial.
translations.idiomatic: an edict honored their household, permanently exempted their family from corvée labor, and provided official funds for the sisters' burial.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹曹陸海著賦以美之。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody to praise them.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody in their praise.

sentences.zh: 又有尉氏尉王泛妻裴氏，儀王傅巨卿之女也。

translations.literal: There was also the wife of Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi, née Pei, daughter of Jujing, Tutor to the Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wang Fan's wife, Lady Pei, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi, daughter of Jujing, Tutor to the Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 素有容範，為賊所俘，賊逼之。

translations.literal: She had always possessed fine bearing and was captured by bandits who pressed her.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for her grace, she was captured by bandits who tried to force her.

sentences.zh: 裴曰：「吾衣冠之子，當死即死，終不茍全一命，受汙於賊。

translations.literal: Pei said, "I am a child of the gentry; when I must die I shall die—I will never cling to life in degradation and suffer defilement by bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei said, "I am a daughter of the gentry; when I must die, I shall die—I will never cling to life in shame and suffer defilement at the hands of bandits."

sentences.zh: 」賊脅之以兵，逼之以罵，裴堅力抗之。

translations.literal: The bandits threatened her with weapons and pressed her with curses; Pei firmly resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits threatened her with weapons and cursed her; Lady Pei resisted with all her strength.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，乃支解裴氏，至死不屈。

translations.literal: The bandits grew furious and dismembered Pei; to her death she did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits dismembered Lady Pei; she did not yield even unto death.

sentences.zh: 季卿亦以狀跡聞。

translations.literal: Jiqing also reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing also reported the circumstances to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「鄭州原武縣尉盧甫亡妻李氏、汴州尉氏縣尉王泛亡妻裴氏等，懿範傳家，柔明植性；

translations.literal: An edict stated, "The late wife of Lu Fu, Assistant Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zhengzhou, née Li, and the late wife of Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi in Bianzhou, née Pei, and others—exemplary models transmitted through their families, gentle clarity planted in their nature;"
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "The late Lu Fu, Assistant Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture, whose wife was Lady Li, and the late Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi in Bian Prefecture, whose wife was Lady Pei, among others—exemplary virtue ran in their families, gentle clarity rooted in their nature;"

sentences.zh: 頃因寇難，克彰義烈。

translations.literal: "in recent times through bandit calamity they fully displayed righteous heroism."
translations.idiomatic: "in recent times, amid the ravages of rebellion, they fully displayed righteous heroism."

sentences.zh: 或請代父死，表因心之孝；

translations.literal: "Some asked to die in their fathers' place, showing filial piety from the heart;"
translations.idiomatic: "Some asked to die in their fathers' place, showing heartfelt filial piety;"

sentences.zh: 或誓逐夫亡，標難奪之節。

translations.literal: "some vowed to follow their husbands in death, marking constancy that could not be wrested away."
translations.idiomatic: "some vowed to follow their husbands in death, marking constancy that none could break."

sentences.zh: 宜膺贈律，俾光休美。

translations.literal: "They should receive posthumous honors according to statute, to make their glorious virtue shine."
translations.idiomatic: "They should receive posthumous honors by statute, that their glorious virtue may shine forth."

sentences.zh: 李氏可贈孝昌縣君，裴氏可贈河東縣君，仍編入史冊。

translations.literal: "Li may be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Xiaochang County, Pei as Lady of Hedong County, and both entered into the historical records."
translations.idiomatic: "Lady Li shall be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Xiaochang County, Lady Pei as Lady of Hedong County, and both shall be entered in the historical records."

sentences.zh: 」瀾、渤亦贈官秩。

translations.literal: Lan and Bo were also granted official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Lan and Bo were also granted official ranks.

sentences.zh: 鄒待征妻簿氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Zou Daizheng, née Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Daizheng's wife, Lady Bo.

sentences.zh: 待征，大歷中為常州江陰縣尉，其妻為海賊所掠。

translations.literal: Daizheng, during the Dali era, served as Assistant Magistrate of Jiangyin in Changzhou; his wife was seized by pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Daizheng served as Assistant Magistrate of Jiangyin in Chang Prefecture during the Dali reign; his wife was seized by pirates.

sentences.zh: 薄氏守節，出待征官誥於懷中，托付村人，使謂待征曰：「義不受辱。

translations.literal: Bo upheld her chastity, took Daizheng's official patent from her bosom, entrusted it to a villager, and had him tell Daizheng, "By righteousness I cannot suffer dishonor."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bo upheld her chastity, took Daizheng's official commission from her bosom, entrusted it to a villager, and had him tell Daizheng, "By righteousness I cannot suffer dishonor."

sentences.zh: 」乃投江而死。

translations.literal: She then cast herself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then threw herself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 賊退潮落，待征於江岸得妻屍焉。

translations.literal: When the pirates retreated and the tide ebbed, Daizheng found his wife's corpse on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates retreated and the tide ebbed, Daizheng found his wife's body on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 江左文士，多著節婦文以紀之。

translations.literal: Literati of the lower Yangtze region mostly composed essays on chaste wives to record her.
translations.idiomatic: Literati of the lower Yangtze region composed many essays on chaste wives to commemorate her.

sentences.zh: 李湍妻。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Tuan.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Li Tuan.

sentences.zh: 湍，吳元濟之軍人也。

translations.literal: Tuan was a soldier in Wu Yuanji's army.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan was a soldier in Wu Yuanji's army.

sentences.zh: 元和中，淮南未平，湍心懷向順，乃急渡氵殷河，東降烏重胤。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era, with Huainan not yet pacified, Tuan harbored thoughts of turning loyal and urgently crossed the Yin River to surrender east to Wu Chongyin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, with Huainan not yet pacified, Tuan harbored loyal intentions and urgently crossed the Yin River to surrender to Wu Chongyin in the east.

sentences.zh: 其妻遂為賊束縛在樹，臠而食之，至死，叫其夫曰：「善事烏僕射。

translations.literal: His wife was then bound to a tree by the rebels, cut to pieces and eaten; until her death she called to her husband, "Serve Vice Director Wu well."
translations.idiomatic: His wife was bound to a tree by the rebels, cut to pieces and eaten alive; until her death she called to her husband, "Serve Vice Director Wu well."

sentences.zh: 」觀者義之。

translations.literal: Onlookers admired her righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it admired her righteousness.

sentences.zh: 至是，重胤以其事請列史冊。

translations.literal: At this time Chongyin requested that her story be entered in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin then petitioned that her story be entered in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 十三年，憲宗下詔從之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Emperor Xianzong issued an edict granting the request.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Emperor Xianzong issued an edict granting the request.

sentences.zh: 董昌齡母楊氏。

translations.literal: The mother of Dong Changling, née Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Changling's mother, Lady Yang.

sentences.zh: 昌齡常為泗州長史，世居於蔡。

translations.literal: Changling had served as Chief Administrator of Sizhou and for generations dwelt in Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Changling had served as Chief Administrator of Si Prefecture; his family had lived in Cai for generations.

sentences.zh: 少孤，受訓於母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he received instruction from his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised and instructed by his mother.

sentences.zh: 累事吳少誠、少陽，至元濟時，為吳房令。

translations.literal: He successively served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang; by Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang; under Yuanji he served as Magistrate of Wu Fang.

sentences.zh: 楊氏潛誡曰：「逆順之理，成敗可知，汝宜圖之。

translations.literal: Yang secretly admonished him, "The principle of rebellion and loyalty, success and failure, can be foreseen—you should plan accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang secretly admonished him, "The principles of loyalty and rebellion, of success and failure, are plain—you must plan accordingly."

sentences.zh: 」昌齡誌未果，元濟又署為郾城令。

translations.literal: Changling's resolve was not yet fulfilled when Yuanji again appointed him Magistrate of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Changling had not yet acted on her counsel when Yuanji appointed him Magistrate of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 楊氏復誡曰：「逆黨欺天，天所不福。

translations.literal: Yang again admonished him, "The rebel faction defies Heaven; Heaven will not bless them."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang admonished him again, "The rebels defy Heaven; Heaven will not bless them."

sentences.zh: 汝當速降，無以前敗為慮，無以老母為念。

translations.literal: "You should surrender quickly; do not worry over past failures, do not think of your aged mother."
translations.idiomatic: "You must surrender quickly; do not worry over past failures, and do not think of your aged mother."

sentences.zh: 汝為忠臣，吾雖歿無恨矣！

translations.literal: "If you become a loyal minister, though I perish I shall have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you become a loyal subject, I shall die without regret!"

sentences.zh: 」及王師逼郾城，昌齡乃以城降，且說賊將鄧懷金歸款於李光顏。

translations.literal: When the imperial army pressed Yancheng, Changling then surrendered the city and also persuaded the rebel general Deng Huaijin to submit to Li Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army besieged Yancheng, Changling surrendered the city and persuaded the rebel general Deng Huaijin to submit to Li Guangyan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗聞之喜，急召昌齡至闕，直授郾城令、兼監察御史，仍賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Xianzong heard of this with joy, urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointed him Magistrate of Yancheng and concurrent Investigating Censor, and further bestowed crimson fish tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was delighted, urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointed him Magistrate of Yancheng and concurrent Investigating Censor, and granted him crimson fish tokens.

sentences.zh: 昌齡泣謝曰：「此皆老母之訓。

translations.literal: Changling wept and thanked him, saying, "This is all my aged mother's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Changling wept and said, "This is all my mother's teaching."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗嗟嘆良久。

translations.literal: Xianzong sighed in admiration for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong sighed in admiration for a long while.

sentences.zh: 元濟囚楊氏，欲殺之，而止者數矣。

translations.literal: Yuanji imprisoned Yang and wished to kill her, but was stopped several times.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji imprisoned Lady Yang and wished to kill her, but was stopped several times.

sentences.zh: 蔡平，楊氏幸無恙。

translations.literal: When Cai was pacified, Yang fortunately remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was pacified, Lady Yang fortunately emerged unharmed.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年，陳許節度使李遜疏楊氏之強明節義以聞，乃封北平郡太君。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, Military Governor Li Xun of Chenxu memorialized Yang's forceful clarity and chaste righteousness; she was then enfeoffed as Grand Mistress of Beiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, Military Governor Li Xun of Chenxu memorialized Lady Yang's wisdom and moral integrity; she was enfeoffed as Grand Mistress of Beiping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 韋雍妻蕭氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Wei Yong, née Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yong's wife, Lady Xiao.

sentences.zh: 雍，故太子賓客。

translations.literal: Yong was a former Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a former Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 張弘靖鎮幽州日，奏授觀察判官，攝監察御史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou he memorialized to appoint him Observation Aide and acting Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hongjing governed You Prefecture, he appointed Yong Observation Aide and acting Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 時屬朝廷制置未備，幽州俗本兇悍，尤不樂文儒為主帥，賓佐習於常態，忿其變通，議論不密，卒然起亂。

translations.literal: At the time the court's arrangements were not yet complete; Youzhou customs were inherently fierce, especially displeased with literary scholars as commanders; aides accustomed to the usual resented his innovations; discussions were not kept secret, and rebellion suddenly arose.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court's arrangements were incomplete; You Prefecture was inherently fierce and especially resented having a literary scholar as commander; aides accustomed to the old ways resented his reforms; loose talk led to sudden rebellion.

sentences.zh: 雍時家亦從劫，蕭氏聞難號呼，專執夫袂，左右格去，以死不從。

translations.literal: Yong's household was also caught in the uprising; Xiao, hearing the calamity, cried out and clung only to her husband's sleeve; attendants pulled her away but she would not follow, preferring death.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's household was caught in the uprising; hearing the commotion, Lady Xiao cried out and clung to her husband's sleeve; attendants pulled her away, but she refused to leave, preferring death.

sentences.zh: 及雍臨刃，蕭氏涕而告曰：「妾不幸年少，義不茍活；

translations.literal: When Yong faced the blade, Xiao wept and said, "I am unfortunate and young; by righteousness I cannot live in degradation;"
translations.idiomatic: As Yong faced the blade, Lady Xiao wept and said, "I am young and unfortunate; by righteousness I cannot live in shame;"

sentences.zh: 今日之事，願先就死！

translations.literal: "in today's affair I wish to die first!"
translations.idiomatic: "in this matter, let me die first!"

sentences.zh: 」執刃者斷其臂而殺雍，蕭氏詞氣不撓，雖兇悍圜視，無不嗟嘆。

translations.literal: The blade-wielder severed her arm and killed Yong; Xiao's words and spirit did not bend, and though the fierce rebels looked on in a circle, none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The assassin severed her arm and killed Yong; Lady Xiao's spirit did not waver, and even the fierce rebels who looked on could not help but sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 其夕，蕭氏亦卒。

translations.literal: That evening Xiao also died.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Lady Xiao died as well.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，節度使楊誌誠表明其事，因降敕追封蘭陵縣君。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, Military Governor Yang Zhicheng reported her deeds, and by edict she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Lanling County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe, Military Governor Yang Zhicheng reported her deeds, and by edict she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Lanling County.

sentences.zh: 衡方厚妻程氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Heng Fanghou, née Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Fanghou's wife, Lady Cheng.

sentences.zh: 方厚，太和中任邕州都督府錄事參軍，為招討使董昌齡誣枉殺之。

translations.literal: Fanghou, during the Taihe era, served as Recorder of the Regional Commander's staff at Yongzhou and was falsely accused and killed by Pacification Commissioner Dong Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Fanghou served as Recorder on the staff of the Yong Prefecture commandery during the Taihe reign and was falsely accused and killed by Pacification Commissioner Dong Changling.

sentences.zh: 程氏力不能免，乃抑其哀，如非冤者。

translations.literal: Cheng, unable by force to prevent it, suppressed her grief and acted as if there were no injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to prevent it by force, Lady Cheng suppressed her grief and acted as if no injustice had occurred.

sentences.zh: 昌齡雅不疑慮，聽其歸葬。

translations.literal: Changling, never suspecting, permitted her to return and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Changling, never suspecting her intentions, permitted her to return home and bury him.

sentences.zh: 程氏故得以徒行詣闕，截耳於右銀臺門，告夫被殺之冤。

translations.literal: Cheng was thus able to travel on foot to court, cut off her ear at the Right Yintai Gate, and report her husband's wrongful killing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng was thus able to travel on foot to the capital, cut off her ear at the Right Yintai Gate, and report her husband's wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 御史臺鞫之，得實，諫官亦有章疏，故昌齡再受譴逐。

translations.literal: The Censorate investigated and found the facts; remonstrating officials also submitted memorials, so Changling was again punished and banished.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate investigated and confirmed the facts; remonstrating officials also submitted memorials, and Changling was again punished and banished.

sentences.zh: 程氏，開成元年降敕曰：「乃者吏為不道，虐殺爾夫，詣闕申冤，徒行萬里，崎嶇逼畏，濱於危亡。

translations.literal: Regarding Cheng, in the first year of Kaicheng an edict stated, "Recently an official acted without the Way and cruelly killed your husband; you came to court to declare your grievance, traveling on foot ten thousand li, through hardship and fear, bordering on peril and death."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Lady Cheng, in the first year of Kaicheng an edict stated, "Recently an official acted without conscience and cruelly killed your husband; you came to court to declare your grievance, traveling on foot ten thousand li through hardship and fear, bordering on death."

sentences.zh: 血誠即昭，幽憤果雪，雖古之烈婦，何以加焉！

translations.literal: "Your blood loyalty is now manifest; your hidden grievance is truly cleared—even fierce women of antiquity, how could they surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: "Your loyal devotion is now manifest; your hidden grievance is truly vindicated—even the heroic women of antiquity could not surpass this!"

sentences.zh: 如聞孤孀無依，晝哭待盡，俾榮祿養，仍賜疏封。

translations.literal: "I hear you are a widowed orphan without support, weeping by day awaiting your end—grant you honorable stipend for support and bestow a noble title."
translations.idiomatic: "I hear you are a widow without support, weeping by day and awaiting your end—grant you an honorable stipend and bestow a noble title."

sentences.zh: 可封武昌縣君，仍賜一子九品正員官。」

translations.literal: "She may be enfeoffed as Lady of Wuchang County, and one son granted a regular ninth-rank post."
translations.idiomatic: "She shall be enfeoffed as Lady of Wuchang County, and one son granted a regular ninth-rank post."

sentences.zh: 女道士李玄真，越王貞之玄孫。

translations.literal: The female Daoist Li Xuanzhen was the great-great-granddaughter of Prince Zhen of Yue.
